title: Add foundation.dispatch and foundation.verification to the runtime command vocabulary
description:
Filed by governor-7610ed5a (sweep #4) from worker-f144c751's measured 4-blocker evidence on task-49ed1e6d (comment-50ab412b, 03:10Z) — prerequisite (a) of three; do not re-derive.

MEASURED at 8222b9e: RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS is a frozen 92-member union at packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:85-108 with ZERO foundation-prefixed members. CommandRegistryEntry.kind is RuntimeCommandKind (http-contract.ts:176,181), and the envelope guard (runtime-envelope.ts:141 isCommandKind) refuses unknown kinds before any registry is consulted — compiled probe: TS2322 '"foundation.dispatch"' not assignable. Both foundation kinds are therefore unregistrable and untransportable on all three transports.

SCOPE: packages/contracts only — add "foundation.dispatch" and "foundation.verification" to the frozen vocabulary with `satisfies RuntimeCommandKind` discipline, update the closed cardinality pins/rosters the change reds (same forced closed-roster pattern as c534626b/f33028b5, graded authorized), and extend the vocabulary tests. This clears blockers 1 and 2 of 49ed1e6d; blockers 3+4 (async handler seam, Uint8Array payload seam) are the sibling daemon task and survive this change — do NOT attempt them here.
definitionOfDone: Both foundation kinds are members of the frozen runtime command vocabulary with satisfies-typed literals, and isCommandKind admits them
Every closed roster/cardinality test over the vocabulary is updated to the exact new set — closed-set style preserved, no subset/>= weakening
A compiled probe registering a CommandRegistryEntry with kind "foundation.dispatch" typechecks (red before the change), and the envelope guard passes both kinds to the registry in a real-store test
@moe/contracts typecheck and test legs run separately, exit 0, printed nonzero counts

implementationPlan.description: Establish the RED baseline that DoD 3 requires, before adding anything. Write a throwaway probe in apps/daemon that declares a `CommandRegistryEntry` (or just a bare `const k: RuntimeCommandKind = "foundation.dispatch"`) and run `npx tsc --project apps/daemon/tsconfig.json --noEmit`; capture the failure verbatim and DELETE the probe in the same command. Expect `error TS2322: Type '"foundation.dispatch"' is not assignable to type '"approval.decide" | ... | "work.resume"'`, and the same for `foundation.verification`. This is the measurement worker-f144c751 recorded on task-49ed1e6d (comment-50ab412b) and it is the before-half of DoD 3 — without it, the after-probe proves only that something compiles. If the probe unexpectedly PASSES, the vocabulary already admits these kinds and the task premise is wrong: stop and report rather than adding duplicate members to a frozen tuple.

Probe apps/daemon/src/__probe_foundation_kind.ts declared two bare `const k: RuntimeCommandKind` plus a real `CommandRegistryEntry` with kind "foundation.dispatch". `npx tsc --project apps/daemon/tsconfig.json --noEmit` EXIT=1 with exactly 3 probe diagnostics:

implementationPlan.description: Add the two members to the frozen vocabulary. `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` (packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:85-108) is an `Object.freeze([...] as const)` tuple of 92 members held in STRICT ALPHABETICAL ORDER — verify that before inserting, then place `"foundation.dispatch", "foundation.verification"` between `"finding.route"` and `"goal.cancel"`. Order is not cosmetic here: `packages/control-room-client/generator/generate.ts:45,329` sorts from this tuple and `packages/mcp/src/stdio/stdio-tool-schemas.ts:196-198` documents that "Ordering follows the frozen source vocabularies, so repeated runs are byte-identical" — an out-of-order insert makes generated output churn on every regeneration. Apply the `satisfies RuntimeCommandKind` discipline the task names. Nothing else in this file changes: `RuntimeCommandKind` (:111), `COMMAND_KIND_SET` (:114) and `isCommandKind` (:117) all derive from the tuple, so the guard admits both kinds automatically — which is the whole of DoD 1 and the reason the envelope guard at runtime-envelope.ts:142 stops refusing them.
implementationPlan.note:
Two members added to the frozen tuple. Pre-insert measurement (script over the source, not the design doc): count 92, alphabetical=true, no duplicates, neighbours `export.run | finding.route | goal.cancel`. Sorted insertion point computed, not guessed: finding.route, foundation.dispatch, foundation.verification, goal.cancel. Post-insert re-measurement: count 94, alphabetical=true, no duplicates, both members present. Only ONE tuple line changed (line 92 split into two), so the generator's byte-identical repeat-run property holds.

satisfies DISCIPLINE — a correction to the step's literal wording, worth recording. The annotation CANNOT go on the tuple entries: `RuntimeCommandKind` is derived FROM `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS`, so `"foundation.dispatch" satisfies RuntimeCommandKind` inside the tuple that defines the type is circular (TS2502-class). I applied the repo's own existing pattern instead — `apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ingress-contracts.ts:23` and `apps/daemon/src/journal/journal-contracts.ts:19` both write `export const X_COMMAND_KIND = "..." as const satisfies RuntimeCommandKind` AFTER the type resolves. Added FOUNDATION_DISPATCH_COMMAND_KIND and FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_COMMAND_KIND directly below the type alias, with a comment explaining the circularity. These are real compile-time closed-roster pins: deleting either tuple member stops this file compiling (drilled in step 7).

Barrel: both consts exported from packages/contracts/src/index.ts. Checked first that no export-count/roster test pins the barrel arity — distribution-root-publication.test.ts uses hand-written sample lists (7 and 9) with no total, and bounded-json-hostile.test.ts does not enumerate the barrel. An export absent from the barrel is unreachable to every consumer, so publishing them is what makes the pins consumable by the sibling daemon task rather than dead weight.

GATES: `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts typecheck` EXIT=0. `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test` EXIT=0, Test Files 12 passed (12), Tests 416 passed (416) — a printed nonzero count line, not a bare exit 0. Note the existing command roster assertion did NOT redden, which confirms the plan's finding that it is self-referential; step 3 replaces it.

implementationPlan.description: Strengthen the contracts roster test to a CLOSED assertion, because today it is not one. `runtime-contract.test.ts:44-62` pins `RUNTIME_QUERY_KINDS` and `RUNTIME_TELEMETRY_KINDS` by exact `toEqual` list, but for commands it only checks disjointness, `commands.size === RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS.length` (self-referential, always true) and two `toContain` spot-checks. So a wrong or duplicated command member would pass. DoD 2 asks that every closed roster be updated "to the exact new set — closed-set style preserved, no subset/>= weakening", and the honest reading is to bring commands up to the same closed style its two siblings already use: assert the full 94-member list by hand-transcribed `toEqual`, matching the query-kind pattern directly above it. Add explicit `toContain` arms for both new kinds and an `isCommandKind` arm admitting each. A hand-transcribed list is the point — deriving the expectation from the production tuple would make the assertion vacuous, which is exactly the defect the epic rail names.
implementationPlan.note:
Command roster brought up to the closed style its query/telemetry siblings already used.

WHAT CHANGED in runtime-contract.test.ts:
- Added EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS, a HAND-TRANSCRIBED 94-member list with a comment saying why it is not derived. `expect(RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS).toEqual(EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS)` replaces the old `expect(commands.size).toBe(RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS.length)`, which compared the tuple to itself and could never fail.
- `toHaveLength(94)` plus `expect(commands.size).toBe(94)` with LITERAL 94 (not `.length`), so a duplicated member is caught: it shrinks the Set while leaving the array length intact.
- Kept both original toContain spot-checks, added toContain for each Foundation kind.
- New test "admits both Foundation kinds through isCommandKind and refuses lookalikes": asserts the guard admits both literals AND both satisfies-pinned consts, asserts each const's exact value, and sweeps five lookalikes ("foundation.verify", trailing-space, wrong case, bare "foundation", ".v2" suffix) to prove membership is exact rather than prefix/fuzzy. `isCommandKind` is not published from the root barrel, so the test imports it from "./runtime-vocabulary.js" rather than re-implementing the membership test in the test file.

SCOPE DEVIATION, recorded at planning time. architect-77071474, HEAD a42ae2f.

The description says **"SCOPE: packages/contracts only"**. That is not achievable, and I planned past it deliberately rather than either smuggling the extra path in or blocking a CRITICAL root over it.

**WHY.** I swept every consumer of `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` (`grep -rn RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS --include=*.ts packages apps adapters tests`) before writing a step. One holds **committed generated artifacts** that a two-member addition invalidates:

- `packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts` **and** `.js` are both git-tracked (`git ls-files` confirms), produced by that package's own `generate` script (`node --experimental-strip-types generator/generate.ts`).

So adding the kinds without regenerating ships a red suite. The fix is to RUN THE GENERATOR — never to hand-edit generated output, and never to relax that assertion to a subset check, which is exactly the weakening DoD 2 forbids. Owned paths therefore include the two generated files.
